LESSON: EXPLORING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Environment and 1.1 Weather and Sky By the end of the sub-strand,  Learners to 
Topic 2.2.2: Exploring

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Exploring. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is the weather today?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EXPLORING
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Exploring helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: EXPLORING
Study Exploring like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe

What this means
In this part you learn to identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Exploring” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Exploring is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Exploring” around your school. (skill: identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Exploring to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Exploring from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Exploring: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Exploring?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is the weather today?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Exploring means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify weather (windy, cloudy, rainy and sunny) conditions of the day  In groups, learners to observe.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
